quote: Firewood becomes ash, and it does not become firewood again.
source: Dōgen, Shōbōgenzō, Genjōkōan, in Enlightenment Unfolds (trans. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi, 1999)
note: The translation is by Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi together, revised at San Francisco Zen Center and later at Berkeley Zen Center, not by Tanahashi alone. Aitken is restored to the credit. The wording is the one printed in Enlightenment Unfolds, Shambhala, 1999. An earlier version stands in Moon in a Dewdrop, 1985, pages 69 to 73.

evidence.where: Read a parallel-translation edition of Genjōkōan that prints the Aitken and Tanahashi text with its own credit line; the sentence and the one after it match, and the credit names both translators and the Enlightenment Unfolds printing.
evidence.edition: Kazuaki Tanahashi, Enlightenment Unfolds, Boston, Shambhala, 1999, pages 35 to 39

reason: The wording is right and the edition is right, but the translation is credited to Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi jointly, and the proposal named only Tanahashi. Dōgen stands at one line for the year, so a second is within the cap.
